# Operating System Principles {.unnumbered}

Part IV examines the operating system and runtime executive of the Stochastic Computer: the control plane that coordinates long-running, stateful trajectories. We formalize trajectory checkpointing and crash recovery across irreversible tool side-effects using Write-Ahead Logs and distributed Sagas, design asynchronous event loops and watchdog timers for preemptive human-in-the-loop intervention, and develop trajectory schedulers under non-deterministic service times and memory constraints.

::: {#pri-vol3-reversibility-sagas .callout-principle title="The reversibility boundary and compensating Sagas"}

**Invariant**: Internal context state is private and freely reversible; external environmental state is shared and often irreversible. Robust failure recovery requires distributed Sagas with deterministic compensating actions.

**Implication**: The agent operating system must stage irreversible operations behind Write-Ahead Logs (WAL), capability leases, and human approval gates treated as high-latency suspension objects.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-preemptive-interrupts .callout-principle title="Preemptive interrupts and watchdog timers"}

**Invariant**: Long-running stochastic reasoning loops are subject to runaway token consumption, infinite loops, and context poisoning; the operating system must possess out-of-band preemption authority.

**Implication**: Runtimes must implement non-blocking event loops, asynchronous signal delivery, and hard watchdog timers that can halt execution independently of model cooperation.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-heavy-tailed-scheduling .callout-principle title="Trajectory-aware scheduling and continuous batching"}

**Invariant**: Agent workloads exhibit heavy-tailed Pareto execution times and bimodal prefill/decode latency structures that break classical synchronous batching models.

**Implication**: Cluster schedulers must combine continuous chunked batching, cache-affinity routing, and disaggregated prefill-decode architectures to prevent head-of-line blocking.

:::
